“It was just chaos,” he said. “You had all types of ships, like other barges and other companies down there trying to help out, which also was a little convoluted because you had people still in the water.”
It appeared the tanker seemed to have “some type of loss of steering,” but the exact cause of the crash was unknown, Coast Guard Capt. Melanie Burnham said.
The National Transportation Safety Board planned to investigate the crash, but members were initially unable to make it to New Orleans because all flights nationwide were grounded due to communications problems at regional air traffic control centers.
Cruise line did a roll call to make sure all were accounted for
The people who weren’t injured were brought to a nearby auditorium, and cruise officials did a roll call to make sure everyone was accounted for, Moreno said.
Many people lost their IDs and even car keys in the disaster. Most were from out of town, the mayor said.
“They needed chargers for their phones. Some people didn’t have phones,” Moreno said. “This has now made national news. They need to contact their families to let them know they’re OK. Food, hotel rooms, transportation.”
The cruise ship was built in 2015 and operated by American Cruise Lines. It is five stories and can hold up to 150 passengers.
The American Heritage was finishing an eight-day cruise to several Mississippi River destinations in Louisiana and Mississippi.
The 520-foot-long (160-meter-long) vessel had a final destination in New Orleans, according to MarineTraffic, and was sailing under a flag for the Marshall Islands.
Expert says catastrophic failure of systems on boat
It’s too early to tell what might have caused the crash, but videos indicate some kind of catastrophic system failure on the vessel and “super bad luck” that it struck the boat as passengers were departing, said Martin Davies, a maritime law expert at Tulane University.
The tanker was traveling upriver, going slowly against the current, Davies said.
“For something like this to happen for an upbound ship indicates that something must have gone really badly wrong,” Davies said.
Tankers have local pilots on board for guidance because they know the waters and the ship very well, and the ship had already made the difficult Algiers Point turn on the Mississippi River before it crashed, Davies said.
Tanker owned by subsidiary of Chinese shipbuilder
The ship is owned by a company called Nave Shipping SA, which is registered in Monrovia, Liberia, according to the International Maritime Organization.
It is a subsidiary of the China State Shipbuilding Corporation, a sprawling Chinese state-owned conglomerate, according to the live shipping tracker MarineTraffic.
The Chinese company overseeing the asphalt tanker in 2022 accounted for nearly a quarter of the global commercial shipbuilding market, according to a report by the Stockholm International Peace Research Institute. It was also the largest military shipbuilder in the world at the time.
China State Shipbuilding Corp. didn’t respond to an emailed request for comment Friday afternoon.
The tanker involved in the crash specializes in carrying large quantities of asphalt and bitumen, a semi-solid substance that is often used for road construction and roofing, according to MarineTraffic.
___
Jeffrey Collins reported from Columbia, South Carolina. Ed White in Detroit, Safiyah Riddle in Los Angeles, M Reo in Washington, D.C., Anna Wilder in Austin, Texas, and Beatrice Dupuy in New York contributed to this report.

‘Miracle on the Mississippi’: No fatalities after tanker crashes into river cruiser near Port of New Orleans
NEW ORLEANS (WVUE) - The American Cruise Lines’ American Heritage sits on its side in the Mississippi River in front of the Port NOLA offices after a tanker allided with the docked river cruiser Friday. Officials said all passengers were accounted for and 32 people were sent to hospitals for non-critical injuries.
Dozens of lights were brought in to illuminate the two disabled ships. Coast Guard boats are at the site along the New Orleans Riverwalk.
The Port of New Orleans press secretary said the Atlantic Asphalt tanker allided with the American Heritage around 12:30 p.m. Friday (Nov. 13).
An allision, different from a collision, is when a moving ship crashes into a stationary one.
The river cruiser was docked on the Mississippi River outside 1350 Port of New Orleans Place when the tanker crashed into it, Port NOLA said. The ship docked two hours earlier to begin passenger disembarkation, Port NOLA said.
Port NOLA said 192 people were aboard the American Heritage. After the impact, passengers were ordered to evacuate.
The ship started filling with water and capsizing. Many passengers fell into the water, and others gripped the side of the boat.
City leaders said harbor police, New Orleans firefighters, neighboring boats and other first responders responded.
“As soon as it was reported, everybody ran to it,” Mayor Helena Moreno said.
Due to the residual delays from the nationwide ground stop, the NTSB will no longer send a board member and will instead send a team of investigators by ground to the scene of the vessel collision in New Orleans. No media briefings are planned at this time. Updates on the investigation will be posted to this account and the investigation webpage: https://t.co/tSMmV7b5Pp
— NTSB Newsroom (@NTSB_Newsroom) November 14, 2026
Capt. Melanie Burnham of the U.S. Coast Guard also spoke about the response.
“We are grateful for all of our partners that showed up immediately. It made a difference in our rescue efforts,” Burnham said.
Passengers sought refuge at the Port NOLA office, feet from the wreck. Port NOLA officials said passengers were brought inside the Port of New Orleans Administration Building.
“We put everyone in the auditorium and we started doing roll call and we started to figure out where everyone was,” Moreno said.
At 2 p.m., Gov. Jeff Landry confirmed he was aware of the incident and was heading to New Orleans.
At 2:10 p.m., Moreno’s communication team said multiple individuals had been rescued, and search-and-rescue operations remained ongoing. Moreno responded to the incident with the following statement:
“Emergency crews are responding to a collision involving a cargo ship and a riverboat cruise ship near the Port of New Orleans. Multiple individuals have been rescued, and search-and-rescue operations remain ongoing. Public safety agencies are coordinating response efforts, with the immediate priority being the safety and rescue of those involved. This remains an active and developing incident. Updates to follow.”
The NOLA Ready team said that for information on people missing in the crash, people can call 311 in New Orleans or 504-539-3266.
At 4:11 p.m., Moreno said all crew and passengers had been accounted for, with no fatalities. She said 32 people were hospitalized and no one was in critical condition.
Officials said cruise passengers will stay at nearby hotels overnight while they work on return trips home.
The Coast Guard is the lead agency investigating how the crash happened. Initial evidence points to issues sailing the tanker.
“There seems to be some kind of loss of steering,” Chief Melanie Montroll of New Orleans Harbor Police said.
Montroll said she expects to have information in the next couple of days.
“I should have information internally and share it with everyone in the next couple of days,” Montroll said.
The National Transportation Safety Board launched a Go Team to investigate the collision. The team is set to arrive Saturday morning (Nov. 14).
The U.S. Coast Guard said its “hearts are with the passengers, crew, and families” affected by the allision. The Coast Guard said the river is closed to all vessel traffic between mile markers 93 and 96.
Coast Guard officials said the Mississippi River could likely reopen to single-lane water traffic in the coming days. Officials have not said when they expect to remove the river cruiser from the crash site.
“My heart is with the survivors, their families, and everyone who witnessed this horrific accident,” Rep. Troy Carter said. Carter is monitoring the situation and said he commends the actions of the emergency response teams.
President Trump thanked the Coast Guard in a post on Truth Social.
“Thank you to the United States Coast Guard for doing such an incredible job of rescue, and other work, having to do with the crash of the two ships in Louisiana,” Trump posted.
“Likewise, all of Law Enforcement and First Responders were fantastic! Incredibly, nobody was killed by this major collision. 32 people are in the hospital. Thank you to Governor Jeff Landry for your outstanding leadership during this very agonizing period of time.”

‘Miracle’: All rescued from capsized New Orleans riverboat in tanker collision
Over 30 people were injured after a tanker collided with a docked riverboat on the Mississippi River near the Port of New Orleans, officials said Friday.
Nearly 200 people were on board the cruise ship, American Heritage, when the Atlantic Asphalt tanker collided with it, according New Orleans officials. All have been accounted for, according to New Orleans Mayor Helena Moreno, calling it a "miracle on the Mississippi."
Thirty passengers from the cruise ship and two officers who ended up the water are hospitalized with non-critical injuries, according to officials. No children were involved, authorities said.
The emergency response began midday Friday, when the tanker "lost control and collided into the cruise ship," Moreno said.
"The passengers began disembarking from the ship after that collision. But while that was happening, the cruise ship began to sink, and then eventually, the cruise ship toppled over and flipped," she said at a news conference Friday afternoon. "Now, when that occurred, we started to have people in the water."
Police began helping evacuate passengers, though not everyone was able to get off before the ship began to capsize, authorities said. The remaining passengers were taken onto various boats to get them to safety, and the search and rescue effort is now over, authorities said.
Moreno praised the rescue effort involving first responders and volunteers.
"At this moment, the information that we have, we have zero people unaccounted for, which truly is a miracle on the Mississippi, and that is a credit to all of the first responders, local, state, federal, who literally jumped right in to help," she said.
The collision occurred at approximately 12:30 p.m. local time Friday, according to the Port of New Orleans. The tanker struck the riverboat broadside and hard, sources said.
The tanker appears to have had "some type of a loss of steering," Burnham said during Friday's news conference.
"The exact reason why, we don't know that," she said.
The cruise ship is "significantly damaged," with a small portion remaining above the water line, according to U.S. Coast Guard Capt. Melanie Burnham.
The incident remains under investigation, Burnham said. The National Transportation Safety Board also said it is launching a team to investigate and should arrive by Saturday morning.
"We are going to get down to the bottom of exactly what happened here, and make sure that we make any adjustments necessary so that the people that travel on the waterways here can can know that they can do so in safety," Louisiana Gov. Jeff Landry said at the news conference.
The riverboat had docked approximately two hours earlier to begin passenger disembarkation, according to the Port of New Orleans.
An American Heritage crew member told ABC News that he felt the boat shake, and initially thought the captain was moving the boat.
"There was a hole with the hull of the other boat in the dining room," said Zayvion, a restaurant manager who did want his last name published. "It was a little chaotic, but our team knew what we were doing."
Zayvion said the crew trains weekly for such a scenario and the team "just stayed calm" and helped guide shaken-up guests to safety.
"A lot of people were just scared, like what's gonna happen, especially as the boat tipped over," he said. "It was scary for a lot of people. Even me, like, when it was tipping, I was like, it was getting real."
American Cruise Lines, the riverboat's operator, said in a statement following the operation that it is "grateful to the U.S. Coast Guard, our crew, and the local first responders on the ground in New Orleans for their tremendous rescue efforts."
"We are getting everyone who was aboard the ship settled into hotels and making sure they have everything they need," the statement continued. "We are also in close contact with the U.S. Coast Guard, New Orleans Police, and other agencies, and will continue to coordinate with them."
Multiple agencies, including the New Orleans Fire Department, the New Orleans Police Department and the U.S. Coast Guard, responded to the scene, officials said.
"The river is closed to all vessel traffic between mile markers 93 and 96 while responders assess the situation and conduct response operations," the U.S. Coast Guard said.
Burnham said the Coast Guard will be evaluating how to reopen the waterway.

About 129 passengers, along with crew members, were aboard when the collision happened.
Port NOLA Harbor Police, the New Orleans Fire Department, New Orleans Police Department, U.S. Coast Guard, and emergency medical personnel responded to the scene. Rescue operations were underway as officials worked to account for everyone aboard and assess injuries.

More than a dozen people had been taken to area hospitals, according to city officials. At least 12 people were reported unaccounted for as rescue efforts continued. Authorities had not yet confirmed the final number of injuries or whether there were any fatalities.
“Our immediate priority is the safety of all passengers, crew members and first responders,” Port NOLA said in a news release. “This remains an active and evolving incident. “Multiple individuals have been rescued, and search-and-rescue operations remain ongoing,” Moreno said in a statement. “Public safety agencies are coordinating response efforts, with the immediate priority being the safety and rescue of those involved.”
President Donald Trump was briefed on the collision, according to a senior White House official.
